title: NEPA has taken light
text: Darkness. The whole street groans at once. Your phone is on 9%.

choices.text: Buy fuel for the small generator (₦4,000)
choices.result: The 'I better pass my neighbour' generator roars to life.
Mosquitoes hold a party in your honour.

title: Fuel scarcity
text: Queues stretch for kilometres. Transport fares double overnight. A man is selling fuel in jerrycans at three times the price.

choices.result: Your wallet weeps, but you move.
Free cardio, courtesy of the economy.

title: Landlord wahala
text: Your landlord sends a message: 'Due to the economy, rent is now two years upfront from next year. Thank you for your understanding.' You do not understand.

then.toast: He agrees to one year. Victory, Abuja style.

else.toast: He doesn't budge. You pay a ₦40,000 'agreement fee'.

choices.text: Pay a 'caution fee' to keep things calm (₦25,000)
choices.result: Peace has a price. It is ₦25,000.

title: Black tax
text: Your phone rings. A relative needs money: school fees for a cousin, hospital bill for an aunt, 'small thing' for a ceremony. Everyone believes you are doing well in Abuja.

choices.result: Blessings pour in over WhatsApp voice notes.
'So Abuja has changed you,' says a voice note. You listen to it twice.

title: Naira devaluation
text: Breaking news: the naira has lost a third of its value overnight. Prices in the market change between breakfast and lunch.

choices.result: You buy a bag of rice before it doubles. Smart, for once.
Your savings are now smaller and nobody even asked you.

title: Owambe invitation
text: A friend's wedding this weekend. Aso-ebi costs ₦25,000. Half of Abuja's middle class will be there.

choices.result: You dance, you eat, you leave with two job leads and a party pack.
Your regards are noted. Your absence is also noted.

title: Tunde calls
text: "Guy, I hear say you dey struggle. Take this small thing. No argue me." Tunde sends money he cannot really afford.

choices.text: Accept, and promise to pay it back
choices.result: Real friends are rarer than dollars.
"You too dey form," he laughs. But he's proud of you.

title: Slim has a 'deal'
text: Slim pulls up in a new Benz. "My guy, why you dey suffer? One client, one week, you go buy your own car. Come Lugbe."

choices.text: Tell him you'll come to Lugbe
choices.result: The address is saved in your phone. It feels heavier than it should.
He drives off laughing. You keep your peace, and your freedom.

title: Prophet Profit's new course
text: Prophet Profit is live on Instaflex: "VIP signals group, ₦100k. Last 10 slots. My students are millionaires!" (His students are mostly people he sells to.)

choices.result: The signals are a screenshot of other people's profits. The group is closed a week later.
Nothing happens. But you feel cleaner.

title: DoubleUp Global
text: Everyone at your office is talking about DoubleUp Global, an 'investment platform' paying 30% a month. Your colleague shows you his dashboard: ₦400,000 profit. It looks real.

choices.result: Your dashboard shows ₦50,000 growing every day. You check it every hour.

choices.text: Walk away. 30% a month is not real.
choices.result: Your colleague calls you 'Mr. Doubting Thomas'. For now.

title: DoubleUp Global: early payout
text: Your DoubleUp dashboard shows ₦65,000. A 'withdraw' button glows. Your colleague says withdrawing 'breaks the compound'.

effects.log: Got out of a Ponzi scheme early, with profit.

choices.result: The money lands. You are one of the lucky early ones. Somebody else will pay for it.
The number on the dashboard is beautiful. Numbers on dashboards always are.
Let it compound, they said.

title: DoubleUp Global has frozen withdrawals
text: "Dear valued investors, due to system upgrade, withdrawals are paused for 30 days." The Telegram group is now admin-only. The office is very quiet.

effects.log: Lost money when a Ponzi scheme collapsed.

choices.result: Expensive lesson. You will never forget it, at least.

title: A contact remembers you
text: Someone you met at an owambe sends a message: their company needs a quick contract done this weekend. Pay is good.

choices.result: Networking: the only investment that pays in referrals.
Rest is also productive. Sometimes.

title: Mrs. Okafor makes a call
text: "I spoke about you to a friend at Delta Crest Oil & Gas. Go and see them. And wear a proper tie."

effects.log: Mrs. Okafor recommended you to an oil company.

choices.result: A referral from someone who means it is worth more than a hundred CVs.

title: Police checkpoint
text: "Stop there! Where are you going? Open your phone." The officer scrolls through your messages. Your Heat is high; they have been looking for people like you.

then.toast: You talk about 'my uncle in the force'. They let you go.

choices.result: The officer's smile is very wide.

then.toast: You escape through a market, but now they know your face.

title: QuickKash collectors
text: You missed a QuickKash repayment. Mr. Felix's team has messaged everyone in your contact list: '{name} is a debtor. Tell them to pay.' Your aunt in the village forwards it to the family group.

effects.log: QuickKash shamed you to your whole contact list.

choices.result: Your boss saw it. Your pastor saw it. Your ex saw it.

title: {partner} is 'billing' you
text: "Babe, my hair don scatter. And my phone screen cracked. Just ₦{amount}, I go pay you back." (They will not pay you back.)

choices.result: Hearts and kisses emojis flood your phone.
"Ok." Just 'Ok'. With a full stop.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} saw the messages. No shouting. They pack a small bag, put your spare key on the table, and leave. Your mutual friends stop replying to your messages too.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} found out about the affair. They smiled and said nothing. That was two weeks ago. Today, it all lands at once.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} found out. They are outside your place. You hear glass breaking before you see them.

choices.text: Lock the door and call for help
Go out and try to calm them down

title: Something isn't right
text: A friend sends you a screenshot. {partner}, at a Maitama lounge, very close to someone who is not you. The timestamp is the night they said they were 'at a vigil'.

choices.result: You talk until 3 a.m. It's not fixed. But it's not over.
You block the number. It hurts more than you thought.

title: Two lines
text: {pregnancy_text}

title: A hard decision
text: Abortion is illegal in Nigeria except to save a woman's life, so it often happens in unsafe places. Unsafe abortion is one of the leading causes of maternal death in the country. A licensed private doctor will do it discreetly, for a lot of money. A backstreet clinic is cheap, and dangerous.

choices.text: Change your mind: keep the baby

title: Family meeting
text: Both families know about the baby. Uncles you have never met are in your parents' sitting room. One word keeps coming up: marriage. Soon.

choices.text: Agree to a quick court wedding (₦150,000)

title: Welcome to the world
text: After a long night at Garki General Hospital, your baby is here. Tiny, loud, perfect. Everything is different now.

title: Bolaji's 'small gist'
text: Bolaji, over drinks: "Don't quote me o. Daddy's friend says {asset} will move big tomorrow. Up." Nobody should know this. He does.

choices.result: Insider information is illegal in real markets. It's also how Nepo Babies get richer.

title: JollofInu is trending
text: A famous (fictional) musician tweets a jollof rice emoji. JollofInu, a meme coin, has jumped 90% in an hour. Your group chats are on fire.

choices.result: Check the Trade app. And remember: what goes up like this comes down like this.

title: JollofInu developers have vanished
text: The JollofInu website is down. The developers' accounts are deleted. 'Rug pull,' says Chirp.

title: Konnect Telecom results
text: Konnect Telecom reports record profits after a data price hike. Customers are furious. Investors are delighted.

title: Union Capital Bank fined
text: The (fictional) Central Bank fines Union Capital Bank for 'irregular forex dealings'. Its shares slide.

title: Account frozen
text: Union Capital Bank has put a Post No Debit restriction on your account. A credit far above your usual range was flagged by compliance. ₦{amount} is on hold. Bring your BVN and explain where the money came from at Union Capital Bank HQ in the CBD. Reviews take two days.

choices.text: Ugh. I'll go to the bank.

choices.result: Forty minutes of hold music, then: "Please visit your branch."

title: EFCC invitation
text: A letter on EFCC letterhead: you are "invited" to the Commission's headquarters in Jabi tomorrow to "shed light on some transactions". Everybody knows what an invitation means.

choices.text: Pay a 'consultant' to make it go away (₦300,000)
